data.body: Correction to finding 3 (reclaim_bridge_history). The macOS 'scratch worktree is not clean' reproduction is an artifact. The test passes an environment that replaces the whole env, so my GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL autocrlf config was dropped for the script's git while the worktree had been checked out CRLF; with the config visible, 'git status --porcelain' is clean (ls-files --eol shows i/lf w/crlf, porcelain ''). On Windows the cause is different and not line endings: the test injects the unrelated ref through a '#!/bin/sh' file named 'git' prepended to PATH. Windows CreateProcess never runs it (no .exe), so the ls-remote counter never fires, refs/heads/unrelated is never created, and the test's rev-parse exits 128. That is a POSIX-shell-stub defect (the posix-shell-stubs class, transhuman-wounded-pangolin's tests/_exe_stub.py helper), not CRLF. infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py has no line-ending defect on this evidence.
